_comment: Accepted UNATTRIBUTED inert verdicts — fixtures whose attribute changed no pixels on the listed platforms and which no other ledger has an opinion about. This is the completeness ratchet behind `jui conformance gate --inert-complete`: an unattributed inert verdict that is NOT here fails the gate (an attribute can otherwise stop rendering and nothing says so), and an entry the measurement no longer supports fails too (a fixed attribute must not keep an excuse on file). Reason 'unreviewed-initial-measurement' marks the backlog — consume it by replacing the reason with the adjudication, or by fixing the platform and letting the entry go stale. An entry whose platform set changes returns to the backlog, because the adjudication was written about a different fact.

entries.reason: adjudicated non-discriminating-probe-value, NOT a platform gap: the fixture's own data section declares boundFontWeight as `class: "Int", defaultValue: 0` — 0 is not a font weight in any of the three type systems, so the binding resolves to a value no platform can turn into a weight, and the static sibling fontWeight__static is measured ACTIVE on all three. codegen-effect --paired at HEAD 2026-08-07 (CI's own arguments, 863 probes) reports no defect for this attribute, so the converter emits the spelling — the inert verdict is a render-stage or fixture-shape fact, not a dropped spelling. Disposition: fixture work (owner D) — the generator should give a bound fontWeight a real weight (the SSoT types it string|number, e.g. 700 or "bold"); until it does, this row measures the probe, not the product. Family: non-discriminating-probe-value.

MEASURED GAP, fixed on both dynamic renderers this train, awaiting re-measurement — owners F and G, both landed. Folded 2026-08-07 from G's ack. The desync was: CODEGEN read the spelling on both declared platforms (sjui checkbox_converter.rb:58-59 emits `iconColor:`; kjui checkbox_component.rb:227-231 maps it to Material's checkmarkColor, its comment noting that for a Material Checkbox the icon IS the tick), which is why codegen-effect --paired reports no defect, while DYNAMIC — the renderer the conformance suite photographs — dropped it on both: ios CheckboxConverter.swift:146-160 built CheckBoxView without passing iconColor even though CheckBoxView.swift:141 already resolves `iconColor ?? (isOn ? checkedColor : uncheckedColor)`, and android's DynamicCheckBoxComponent had no reference to it at all. G fixed the android side in KotlinJsonUI c9f7ac5 by adopting the codegen's checkmarkColor mapping rather than inventing a second opinion, removing the colour `when` ladder in favour of Material's Color.Unspecified leave-as-is convention. G's warning, recorded here because the next lane to touch this will hit it: reading CheckboxDefaults.colors() defaults and passing them back is WRONG — in material3 1.4.0 `uncheckedColor` maps to uncheckedBorderColor and uncheckedBoxColor is pinned Transparent, so putting the box colour there erases the unchecked border. Verified by unit only (dynamic 375 + library 199 green, Debug and Release compile green); NO device re-measure — the row drops on the 3PF run, and if it survives, the fix did not reach the draw. Family: icon-tint-dynamic-desync.

adjudicated on the path the fixture actually renders through, AND a codegen/dynamic divergence worth F's attention. The ios conformance lane renders DYNAMIC, and SwiftJsonUI's IndicatorConverter.swift:33-34 returns EmptyView() whenever animating == false — it never reads hidesWhenStopped at all (no read site in that file). Control (stopped) and fixture (stopped, hidesWhenStopped:false) are therefore both empty and the inert verdict is structurally required. The CODEGEN path disagrees with that: sjui_tools indicator_converter.rb:19-30 defaults the attribute to true (matching UIKit) and, for the false face, keeps a zero-opacity spinner in the layout precisely so the surrounding layout still reflows — its own comment says that reflow is 'the whole reason the attribute exists'. So the two ios paths implement different rules for this spelling. Owner F: make the dynamic Indicator honour hidesWhenStopped:false the way codegen does. Even then this fixture cannot show it — the observable is a NEIGHBOUR being reflowed and the fixture has no neighbour (owner D). Family: reflow-only-observable.

F fixed both in e11f8ee: the array form is read first through the typed accessor (the dictionary form stays as the legacy shape the tools emit), all five directions are implemented with Vertical as the declared default, and an explicit startPoint/endPoint inside the dictionary form outranks direction (the more specific declaration wins the axis it speaks about, same precedence shape as the size topic). SECOND, INDEPENDENT defect on the CODEGEN side for this value: 'BottomToTop' has no case arm — modifier_helper.rb:16-23 implements only 'Horizontal' and 'Oblique' and everything else falls through to the vertical emit, so this declared value currently emits what Vertical emits. The SSoT says these two reversed directions are deliberately NOT aliased to Horizontal/Vertical because folding them would reverse the gradient, which makes the missing arm an implementation gap rather than a spelling question. F implemented the value on the dynamic side and DELIBERATELY did not mirror the codegen's fallback — matching a defect on the second path would produce the 'both wrong in the same direction reads as green' shape this campaign has already been bitten by, so the two ios paths differ on purpose until B lands the arm, pinned by a unit test that asserts it does not resolve to Vertical. B: add the arms (.trailing->.leading / .bottom->.top). CODEGEN SIDE IS STILL OPEN and B measured why: whenever `background` is declared alongside `gradient` — which this fixture does — the gradient is invisible on ios through TWO distinct paths, not one. A View with children takes the bag path and emits `.background(<color>)` then `.background(LinearGradient(...))`, and SwiftUI puts the later background further back, so the opaque colour hides it; a childless View takes the Rectangle path and emits `Rectangle().fill(<color>)` followed by the gradient background, which never passes through MODIFIER_ORDER at all. CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S EARLIER HANDOFF: the MODIFIER_ORDER adjacency I flagged is only the first of those two paths, and it is NOT a codegen/dynamic divergence — F measured the dynamic path applying background before gradient in the same order, so if the ordering is changed it must be changed on both paths in one move. B cannot land either fix without a canon ruling: the SSoT declares no precedence between `background` and `gradient`. OPEN QUESTION FOR E: when both are declared, which wins — or does the gradient composite over the background? The row drops when a 3PF run measures ios active; F has not re-measured on device. Family: gradient-dynamic-array-form.
